name: Addison Rae
label: Columbia
lede: Addison Rae went from TikTok dance videos to a shelved first album, a leaked demo Charli xcx wanted a verse on, and a 2025 debut Pitchfork put at No. 12 for the year.

eras.title: Dance videos, then a single that flopped
eras.text: Addison Rae Easterling came up on TikTok, then went at pop through the front door in 2021. The single got flattened, the album behind it was shelved, and she has said she nearly quit.

years.h: Addison Rae posts her first dances in July and leaves LSU by November
years.p: A Lafayette, Louisiana dancer who had competed since age six, she passed a million followers within months. Netflix's He's All That followed in August 2021.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, she joined TikTok in July 2019 posting dance videos to trending songs, left Louisiana State University that November, and signed with the WME talent agency in January 2020.

Her feature debut in Netflix's He's All That in August 2021 was the platform's most-streamed film that week. That is the fame the music later argues with.

years.cap: Rae in a Pandora ME promo shoot, December 2021
years.src: Wikipedia: Obsessed (Addison Rae song) · Wikipedia: AR (EP)
years.h: Critics flatten “Obsessed,” and the album behind it goes in a drawer
years.p: Her debut single, produced by [[Benny Blanco|5a6131f9-f8db-4722-b4d7-6a0c7183c590]], was meant to lead a full album. She has said the reviews nearly made her quit music.
years.xp:
Released March 19, 2021 through Sandlot Records, “Obsessed” had a video directed by Diane Martel and reached the sixth spot on YouTube's trending list on release day. Critics were mostly unkind; one wrote that she "should stick to lip syncing."

Work on an album with producers including Blanco and Charli xcx, reportedly four songs deep by June 2021, was put away. A 2023 British Vogue piece later called the single "fabulously camp."

eras.title: The shelved songs get out
eras.text: The songs she'd put away leaked anyway, and the internet liked them better than it had liked the single. Fans, and one very famous pop star, talked her back in.

years.cap: Rae with Charli xcx at the Pandora ME launch, New York
years.src: Wikipedia: AR (EP) · Wikipedia: 2 Die 4 (song) · Weverse Magazine
years.h: Demos from the abandoned album leak and spread
years.p: Snippets of “I Got It Bad,” “2 Die 4” and “Nothing On (But the Radio)” went viral, and a cult following formed around them.
years.xp:
"Nothing On (But the Radio)" was a song originally recorded by [[Lady Gaga|650e7db6-b795-4eb5-a702-5ea2fc46c848]]. "2 Die 4" leaked as a solo demo and spread on TikTok, despite Rae's hesitation about putting music out after the reaction to "Obsessed."

[[Charli xcx|260b6184-8828-48eb-945c-bc4cb6fc34ca]] had been working with Rae on the album. Rae's account of the text: "I heard '2 Die 4' leaked. You know I love that song. Let me do a verse."

years.h: AR arrives with four lost songs and a Charli verse
years.p: Released through Sandlot Records as a gift to the fans who had kept the leaks alive, it opened with 6.6 million Spotify streams and No. 19 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.
years.xp:
Rae announced the EP on August 14, 2023. "2 Die 4" carried Charli xcx's added verse, the start of a run of collaborations between them.

Weverse Magazine reports Rae framed it as a thank-you to loyal fans, not a comeback.

eras.title: Charli's summer, then Columbia
eras.text: A verse on a Charli xcx remix put her back in front of people. A binder of colors and a first session with two MXM Music writers gave her a sound, and the Columbia debut single became her first Hot 100 entry.

years.h: Rae's scream on the “Von Dutch” remix puts her in Charli's brat summer
years.p: [[A. G. Cook|b12ef43e-72ad-43d0-b216-a8cd32f78852]] reworked Charli xcx's track with a Rae verse, and she ad-libbed the scream that people quote back.
years.xp:
The remix became the first promotional single from Brat and It's Completely Different but Also Still Brat. Rae joined Charli at Madison Square Garden on September 23, 2024 on the Sweat tour.

Rae says Charli trusting her with the lyrics gave her the confidence to make her own album.

years.cap: Directed by Sean Price Williams, modeled on a 1965 film
years.h: “Diet Pepsi” is the first song Rae writes with her producers
years.p: Elvira Anderfjärd and [[Luka Kloser|af77a56e-b8bd-4e9e-a39c-582aeb0637a2]] of Max Martin's MXM Music met Rae in LA in February 2024. Kloser played piano and all three started humming the chorus.
years.xp:
Columbia CEO Ron Perry signed her in late 2023 after she pitched him with a binder of colors, words and performance images instead of demos.

It debuted at No. 54 on the Hot 100 and peaked at No. 10 on the UK Singles Chart. The video, black and white and modeled on the 1965 film Faster, Pussycat! Kill! Kill!, was directed by Sean Price Williams. Critics kept comparing the sound to early [[Lana Del Rey|b7539c32-53e7-4908-bda3-81449c367da6]].

years.cap: Rae on opening night of The Addison Tour, Dublin
years.h: “Aquamarine” gets a Paris video and an Arca reggaeton remix
years.p: The deep-house track had been teased from a pool video during Charli's Brat show in LA. [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]] followed on November 15 with “Arcamarine.”
years.xp: Rae has said she loved the word and the color and wanted a song that captured the feeling. Directed by Sean Price Williams, the video has her shedding layers of clothing, which she described as a journey away from fear of judgment.

eras.title: Addison
eras.text: The debut album came out in June, reached No. 4 in the US and No. 2 in the UK, and landed on year-end lists from Pitchfork to The Washington Post.

years.h: Mitch Ryan films “High Fashion” in Rae's home state
years.p: The third single, co-written with Kloser, Anderfjärd and Tove Burman, was shot in New Orleans.
years.xp: Rolling Stone ranked it No. 21 on its 100 Best Songs of 2025. Rae told Vogue France it was in the spirit of “Diet Pepsi” but more intense.

years.h: “Headphones On” is cut in Stockholm and filmed in Iceland
years.p: Trip-hop with new jack swing in it. The Reykjavík video has Rae as a supermarket worker who imagines riding a horse.
years.xp: Rae has called it one of her most emotional songs and recorded it in Stockholm while ill. The Atlantic's Spencer Kornhaber called it the year's best pop song; Dazed ranked its video No. 1 of 2025.

years.src: Wikipedia: Addison Rae · Wikipedia: Von Dutch (song)
years.h: Rae plays Coachella and Charli joins her for “Von Dutch”
years.p: Arca is part of the set. It is her first Coachella, two months before the album.

years.cap: Rae and dancers on The Fame and Glory Show stage, Dublin
years.src: Wikipedia: Addison (album) · Album of the Year · Year-End Lists · GRAMMY.com
years.h: Pitchfork gives Addison an 8.0 and ranks it No. 12 of the year
years.p: Meaghan Garvey's review compared Rae to Lana Del Rey, Madonna and mostly Britney. She made it with Anderfjärd and Kloser in LA, New York and Sweden.
years.xp:
Every track was written and produced with Anderfjärd and Kloser. They cite Madonna's Ray of Light as a touchstone and built the sound around a Korg M1 synth. Rae's rainbow mood board of aqua, hot pink and yellow shaped the palette, and the cover shows her as a child in sunglasses indoors.

Pitchfork gave it 8.0 (per Wikipedia and Album of the Year) and placed it at No. 12 on its 50 Best Albums of 2025. It debuted at No. 4 on the Billboard 200 with 48,500 units and reached No. 2 in the UK; The Fader and The Washington Post both put it at No. 1 for the year.

years.big: "I enjoy fame. It's very exposing and raw, though you pay a price."
years.src: Wikipedia: Fame Is a Gun · Wikipedia: Addison Rae
years.h: “Fame Is a Gun” is the fifth and last single
years.p: Rae told the Guardian, which named her artist of the year. The video has her hosting a dinner party in a blonde wig and pink trench coat.
years.xp: Written with Kloser and Anderfjärd at Jungle City studio. The song went to No. 3 on Billboard's Hot Dance/Pop Songs and ranked No. 22 on Billboard's 100 Best Songs of 2025.

years.src: Stereogum: Charli xcx · Wikipedia: Von Dutch (song)
yt: Addison Rae w/ Charli XCX live, Greek Theatre
years.h: Charli xcx walks out at the Greek Theatre to close the LA run
years.p: The two friends play the leaked song and the remix that started it.
years.xp: The Addison Tour, her first headline run, ran August to November 2025 across Europe, North America and Australia. Stereogum reported Charli's cameo, and fans filmed it.

years.cap: Rae on The Addison Tour, Coca-Cola Coliseum, Toronto, October 8, 2025
years.h: A Best New Artist nomination, then a slot in the Grammys medley
years.p: Rae performed “Fame Is a Gun” with the other nominees at the 68th Grammys.
years.xp: The Fader said she "won" the medley. The Washington Post ranked her performance third best of the ceremony.
